policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV renders the Old Testament form 'Boaz' at both occurrences and carries no note on the name here, so the English cannot distinguish the Greek spellings Boes/Boos/Booz; base fallback retained.
ASV renders 'Obed' at both occurrences with no note on the name, so the English does not distinguish Iobed from Obed; base fallback retained.
ASV calls David 'the king' once, in the first clause, and the second clause reads simply 'And David begat Solomon'; the added ho basileus of the longer reading is not rendered.

The mapped notes at 1:7 and 1:8 read 'Greek Asaph', so the ASV's underlying text had Asaph and the Asa reading (r02) is excluded; r00-base and r01 are the same Asaph wording and the English cannot choose between them.

Both mapped notes at 1:10 read 'Greek Amos' against the text's 'Amon', so the underlying text had Amos and r02 (Amon) is excluded; r00-base and r01 are the same Amos wording and the English cannot choose between them.

ASV text reads 'the birth of Jesus Christ' and its textual_variant note relegates the shorter reading to the margin ('Some ancient authorities read of the Christ'), so Iesou stood in the text rendered.

'birth' renders genesis and gennesis alike; the only note bearing on the word is classed alternative_rendering ('Or, generation: as in verse 1') and so speaks to English wording, not to a reading. Base fallback retained.
ASV joins the clauses with a colon and no connective; an untranslated gar is not a distinction the English makes either way, and no note is mapped here. Base fallback retained.
'to make her a public example' renders deigmatisai and the compound paradeigmatisai identically, and no note is mapped here; base fallback retained.
ASV reads 'Mary' for either the declined Marian or the indeclinable Mariam; the only note ('Greek begotten') bears on 'conceived', not the name. Base fallback retained.
'by the Lord' renders hypo kyriou with or without the article, which English cannot show, and no note is mapped here; base fallback retained.
'And Joseph arose from his sleep' renders egertheis and the compound diegertheis alike, and no note is mapped here; base fallback retained.
ASV reads 'brought forth a son', without the possessive or 'firstborn' that the longer reading ton huion autes ton prototokon requires; the English renders the short reading.
